articles.author: Md Abdur Rakib
articles.description:
Introducing "Our Social" — A Social Media Platform Built for Feature Phone Users
Introducing "Our Social" — A Social Media Platform Built for Feature Phone Users
Website: Our Social
What Makes Our Social Different? 
Millions of people still rely on basic feature phones and low-speed internet connections, for whom mainstream platforms like Facebook or Instagram are practically unusable. Our Social was built to bridge that gap. The platform runs entirely without JavaScript, meaning it loads smoothly on any basic browser — even on the oldest of devices. Pages are lightweight and fast, even on slow 2G or 3G connections.
Features You'll Love
Our Social offers everything you'd expect from a social network — posting text and images, adding friends, sending messages, liking and commenting on posts, real-time chat, and notifications. The interface is inspired by the classic button-version of Facebook, keeping things simple, familiar, and easy to navigate on small screens.
Browse Without an Account
One of Our Social's standout features is that anyone can browse public profiles and posts without needing to log in. Creating a free account is only required when you want to post, like, comment, or connect with others.
Who Can Join?
Anyone can sign up for free. Whether you're on a feature phone, an old Android device, or any browser-equipped gadget, Our Social works seamlessly for you.
articles.title: Introducing "Our Social" — A Social Media Platform Built for Feature Phone Users

articles.author: CodeWithIshwar
articles.description:
AI tools are becoming increasingly capable of generating code.
They can already produce functions, classes, and sometimes even entire applications.
But they still rely on humans to define some crucial things:
the real problem
the constraints
the trade-offs
the system behavior
AI can generate code quickly, but it still needs developers to understand the context and purpose of the system.
As coding becomes easier with AI assistance, problem definition and system thinking may become even more important skills.
The future developer may not necessarily be the fastest coder.
It may be the person who understands the *problem space deeply and can reason about solutions clearly.

Curious how other developers see this evolving as AI tools continue improving.
CodeWithIshwar
Ishwar Chandra Tiwari
articles.title: AI May Write Code, But Developers Still Define the Problem

I wanted a glanceable counter, always visible.
So I built one.

The first version took two days. SwiftUI's MenuBarExtra made it trivial to get something on screen. I was proud of it.
Then I checked Activity Monitor.
56 MB of memory. For a menu bar app that displays a single number.
I tried to optimize — removed animations, simplified views, cached aggressively. Nothing moved the needle. The SwiftUI runtime itself was the cost. MenuBarExtra allocates a full SwiftUI rendering pipeline whether you need it or not.
For a "set and forget" menu bar app that runs 24/7, 56MB felt like a tax I shouldn't be…
